# Meeting Room Booking System — Requirements Specification (v0.1)

**Status:** Draft · **Owner:** Technical Lead · **Date:** 2026-11 · **Applies to:** v1 (single shared dataset)

> **How to read this document.** This is the single source of truth for the build. Sections 1–2 define data; Section 3 gives the exact, verbatim workflow wording the UI and the tests must use; Section 4 states the two hard, non-negotiable rules; Section 5 gives acceptance criteria the tester will verify; Section 6 records assumptions made pending user answers. Nothing here blocks development — every open question has a stated default.

---

## 1. Scope

Replace the team's shared spreadsheet with a booking system that (a) always shows accurate availability, (b) prevents double bookings, and (c) removes a slot the moment a booking is cancelled. The spreadsheet's two failure modes — double bookings and stale records after cancellation — are the primary defects this system must eliminate.

**In scope (v1):** check availability, make a booking, cancel a booking, single shared dataset across teams.
**Out of scope (v1):** recurring bookings, per-team isolation/authentication tiers, room equipment inventory management, calendar invites/notifications, approvals workflow.

---

## 2. Core entities

### 2.1 Room

| Field | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string (slug/uuid) | yes | Stable, unique, immutable. |
| `name` | string | yes | Human-readable, unique. |
| `capacity` | integer > 0 | yes | Max attendees. |
| `location` | string | no | e.g. floor/building. |
| `amenities` | list of string | no | e.g. `["projector","whiteboard"]`; defaults to `[]`. |
| `active` | boolean | yes | Default `true`. Inactive rooms are hidden from booking but existing bookings remain valid. |

### 2.2 Booking

| Field | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string (uuid) | yes | Assigned by system. |
| `room_id` | reference → Room.id | yes | Must reference an active room at creation time. |
| `title` | string | yes | Purpose of the meeting. |
| `organiser` | string (email/ID) | yes | The person who booked. |
| `attendees` | integer ≥ 1 | no | Default `1`; must be ≤ room capacity (warning, see AC-8). |
| `start` | datetime (ISO-8601, UTC, slot-aligned) | yes | Inclusive start of the half-open interval. |
| `end` | datetime (ISO-8601, UTC, slot-aligned) | yes | Exclusive end; must be `> start`. |
| `status` | enum: `confirmed` \| `cancelled` | yes | Default `confirmed`. |
| `created_at` | datetime (UTC) | yes | Set by system. |
| `cancelled_at` | datetime (UTC) \| null | no | Set when status becomes `cancelled`. |
| `cancel_reason` | string \| null | no | Optional (pending Q5). |
| `cancelled_by` | string \| null | no | Who performed the cancellation. |

**Interval convention (fixed, do not change):** a booking occupies the **half-open interval `[start, end)`**. Two intervals overlap **iff** `a.start < b.end AND b.start < a.end`. This convention is what makes back-to-back bookings legal (see Rule R1).

---

## 3. User workflows (exact wording)

These three strings are the canonical descriptions. UI copy and test names must match the intent exactly.

### WF-1 — Check availability
> **"Check availability":** the user selects a room and a date (or a time range) and sees every bookable slot for that room on that day, each slot marked as **available** or **booked**. A slot is shown as available if and only if no booking with status `confirmed` covers it. Cancelled bookings must never appear as blocking.

### WF-2 — Book a room
> **"Book a room":** the user picks an available slot for a room, enters a title and organiser (and optionally attendees), and confirms. If the slot is still free at confirmation time, the system creates a `confirmed` booking and the slot immediately shows as booked for everyone else. If the slot is no longer free, the system refuses the booking with a clear conflict message and creates nothing.

### WF-3 — Cancel a booking
> **"Cancel a booking":** the user opens an existing booking and cancels it (optionally giving a reason, if permitted). After cancellation the booking's status becomes `cancelled` and its slot is **immediately** shown as available again in WF-1 for every user.

---

## 4. Hard rules (non-negotiable)

- **R1 — No overlapping confirmed bookings.** For the same room, two bookings with status `confirmed` may **never** overlap in time: for any two such bookings `a`, `b` where `a.room_id == b.room_id`, it must hold that `NOT (a.start < b.end AND b.start < a.end)`. Back-to-back bookings (`a.end == b.start`) are **allowed**. The check must be enforced **atomically at write time** so two simultaneous requests cannot both succeed (no check-then-write race). On failure the system returns a conflict error and persists nothing.
- **R2 — Cancellation frees the slot immediately; no stale records.** A cancelled booking must free its slot synchronously: any availability query (WF-1) issued *after* a cancellation returns must show that slot as available, with no delay, cache, or background reconciliation. Cancelled bookings are retained only as history and must be excluded from every availability/blocking view. There must be no state in which a cancelled booking blocks a slot.

---

## 5. Acceptance criteria

Testable criteria; the tester verifies each against WF-1/WF-2/WF-3 and R1/R2.

| ID | Criterion |
|---|---|
| **AC-1** | Availability (WF-1) lists exactly the slots in the room's working hours, each marked available/booked correctly. |
| **AC-2** | A booking whose `[start,end)` does not overlap any confirmed booking for that room is created with status `confirmed`. |
| **AC-3 (R1)** | A booking attempt that would overlap an existing confirmed booking for the same room is rejected with a conflict error and persists **zero** records. |
| **AC-4 (R1)** | Two confirmed bookings for the same room can never be in an overlapping state — verified by concurrent booking attempts, where at most one succeeds. |
| **AC-5 (R1)** | Back-to-back bookings (`a.end == b.start`) are **accepted**. |
| **AC-6 (R1)** | Partial overlaps (start inside another, end inside another, one fully contained) are all **rejected**. |
| **AC-7 (R2)** | After a cancellation, a subsequent WF-1 call shows the freed slot as available immediately (same request cycle; no wait). |
| **AC-8** | A cancelled booking never blocks any future booking of the same room and never appears as "booked" in availability. |
| **AC-9 (WF-3)** | Cancelling sets `status=cancelled` and records `cancelled_at`; the record is retained for history but excluded from blocking views. |
| **AC-10** | `end > start` is enforced; `start`/`end` are slot-aligned and stored in UTC; `attendees ≤ capacity` produces a warning (not a hard block) when configured as such. |
| **AC-11 (WF-2)** | A successful booking immediately appears as booked to all other users on the next availability read (no stale cache). |
| **AC-12** | All three workflows are reachable end-to-end with the exact wording in Section 3. |

---

## 6. Assumptions (explicit, pending user answers)

Made so the developer is not blocked. Each maps to a chat question above; all are cheap to change if the user replies.

| # | Question | Assumed default |
|---|---|---|
| A1 | Rooms & capacities | 3 seed rooms: `Small (4)`, `Medium (8)`, `Large (12)`; same hours. Data-driven, so easily replaced. |
| A2 | Granularity | Fixed **30-minute slots**; bookings are start/end on slot boundaries. |
| A3 | Working hours / timezone | Bookable **09:00–18:00, Mon–Fri**, in **Asia/Hong_Kong (UTC+8)**; all times stored in **UTC**. |
| A4 | Max duration | **4 hours** per booking. |
| A5 | Cancellation authority | **Organiser or admin only**; `cancel_reason` **optional**. |
| A6 | Recurring bookings | **Not supported in v1** (single bookings only). |
| A7 | Overlap/back-to-back | **Back-to-back allowed**; only true overlaps forbidden (R1). |
| A8 | Team model | **Multi-team, single shared dataset**, no per-team isolation or approval. |

> ⚠️ If any answer contradicts a default, the affected section (2, 3, 4, or 5) is updated and this table is marked resolved. Assumptions A1–A8 are **configuration-level**, so no code rewrite is required to change them.

---

## 7. Downstream hand-off

- **Developer:** implement entities per Section 2, the atomic overlap guard per R1, and the synchronous cancellation per R2; expose WF-1/WF-2/WF-3 exactly as worded.
- **Tester:** treat Section 5 as the test plan; AC-4 requires a **concurrency** test, AC-6 a **partial-overlap matrix**, AC-7/AC-8 the **no-stale-record** checks.

---

**Deliverable status:** Complete as an inline markdown document. Open questions posted to the team (top of message); all defaults documented (Section 6) so development and testing can start immediately. Once the user answers, I will reconcile Sections 2–6 against their replies and hand a frozen v1.0 to the developer.

# Meeting Room Booking System — Requirements Specification (v0.1)

**Status:** Draft · **Owner:** Technical Lead · **Date:** 2026-11 · **Applies to:** v1 (single shared dataset)

> **How to read this document.** This is the single source of truth for the build. Sections 1–2 define data; Section 3 gives the exact, verbatim workflow wording the UI and the tests must use; Section 4 states the two hard, non-negotiable rules; Section 5 gives acceptance criteria the tester will verify; Section 6 records assumptions made pending user answers. Nothing here blocks development — every open question has a stated default.

---

## 1. Scope

Replace the team's shared spreadsheet with a booking system that (a) always shows accurate availability, (b) prevents double bookings, and (c) removes a slot the moment a booking is cancelled. The spreadsheet's two failure modes — double bookings and stale records after cancellation — are the primary defects this system must eliminate.

**In scope (v1):** check availability, make a booking, cancel a booking, single shared dataset across teams.
**Out of scope (v1):** recurring bookings, per-team isolation/authentication tiers, room equipment inventory management, calendar invites/notifications, approvals workflow.

---

## 2. Core entities

### 2.1 Room

| Field | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string (slug/uuid) | yes | Stable, unique, immutable. |
| `name` | string | yes | Human-readable, unique. |
| `capacity` | integer > 0 | yes | Max attendees. |
| `location` | string | no | e.g. floor/building. |
| `amenities` | list of string | no | e.g. `["projector","whiteboard"]`; defaults to `[]`. |
| `active` | boolean | yes | Default `true`. Inactive rooms are hidden from booking but existing bookings remain valid. |

### 2.2 Booking

| Field | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string (uuid) | yes | Assigned by system. |
| `room_id` | reference → Room.id | yes | Must reference an active room at creation time. |
| `title` | string | yes | Purpose of the meeting. |
| `organiser` | string (email/ID) | yes | The person who booked. |
| `attendees` | integer ≥ 1 | no | Default `1`; must be ≤ room capacity (warning, see AC-8). |
| `start` | datetime (ISO-8601, UTC, slot-aligned) | yes | Inclusive start of the half-open interval. |
| `end` | datetime (ISO-8601, UTC, slot-aligned) | yes | Exclusive end; must be `> start`. |
| `status` | enum: `confirmed` \| `cancelled` | yes | Default `confirmed`. |
| `created_at` | datetime (UTC) | yes | Set by system. |
| `cancelled_at` | datetime (UTC) \| null | no | Set when status becomes `cancelled`. |
| `cancel_reason` | string \| null | no | Optional (pending Q5). |
| `cancelled_by` | string \| null | no | Who performed the cancellation. |

**Interval convention (fixed, do not change):** a booking occupies the **half-open interval `[start, end)`**. Two intervals overlap **iff** `a.start < b.end AND b.start < a.end`. This convention is what makes back-to-back bookings legal (see Rule R1).

---

## 3. User workflows (exact wording)

These three strings are the canonical descriptions. UI copy and test names must match the intent exactly.

### WF-1 — Check availability
> **"Check availability":** the user selects a room and a date (or a time range) and sees every bookable slot for that room on that day, each slot marked as **available** or **booked**. A slot is shown as available if and only if no booking with status `confirmed` covers it. Cancelled bookings must never appear as blocking.

### WF-2 — Book a room
> **"Book a room":** the user picks an available slot for a room, enters a title and organiser (and optionally attendees), and confirms. If the slot is still free at confirmation time, the system creates a `confirmed` booking and the slot immediately shows as booked for everyone else. If the slot is no longer free, the system refuses the booking with a clear conflict message and creates nothing.

### WF-3 — Cancel a booking
> **"Cancel a booking":** the user opens an existing booking and cancels it (optionally giving a reason, if permitted). After cancellation the booking's status becomes `cancelled` and its slot is **immediately** shown as available again in WF-1 for every user.

---

## 4. Hard rules (non-negotiable)

- **R1 — No overlapping confirmed bookings.** For the same room, two bookings with status `confirmed` may **never** overlap in time: for any two such bookings `a`, `b` where `a.room_id == b.room_id`, it must hold that `NOT (a.start < b.end AND b.start < a.end)`. Back-to-back bookings (`a.end == b.start`) are **allowed**. The check must be enforced **atomically at write time** so two simultaneous requests cannot both succeed (no check-then-write race). On failure the system returns a conflict error and persists nothing.
- **R2 — Cancellation frees the slot immediately; no stale records.** A cancelled booking must free its slot synchronously: any availability query (WF-1) issued *after* a cancellation returns must show that slot as available, with no delay, cache, or background reconciliation. Cancelled bookings are retained only as history and must be excluded from every availability/blocking view. There must be no state in which a cancelled booking blocks a slot.

---

## 5. Acceptance criteria

Testable criteria; the tester verifies each against WF-1/WF-2/WF-3 and R1/R2.

| ID | Criterion |
|---|---|
| **AC-1** | Availability (WF-1) lists exactly the slots in the room's working hours, each marked available/booked correctly. |
| **AC-2** | A booking whose `[start,end)` does not overlap any confirmed booking for that room is created with status `confirmed`. |
| **AC-3 (R1)** | A booking attempt that would overlap an existing confirmed booking for the same room is rejected with a conflict error and persists **zero** records. |
| **AC-4 (R1)** | Two confirmed bookings for the same room can never be in an overlapping state — verified by concurrent booking attempts, where at most one succeeds. |
| **AC-5 (R1)** | Back-to-back bookings (`a.end == b.start`) are **accepted**. |
| **AC-6 (R1)** | Partial overlaps (start inside another, end inside another, one fully contained) are all **rejected**. |
| **AC-7 (R2)** | After a cancellation, a subsequent WF-1 call shows the freed slot as available immediately (same request cycle; no wait). |
| **AC-8** | A cancelled booking never blocks any future booking of the same room and never appears as "booked" in availability. |
| **AC-9 (WF-3)** | Cancelling sets `status=cancelled` and records `cancelled_at`; the record is retained for history but excluded from blocking views. |
| **AC-10** | `end > start` is enforced; `start`/`end` are slot-aligned and stored in UTC; `attendees ≤ capacity` produces a warning (not a hard block) when configured as such. |
| **AC-11 (WF-2)** | A successful booking immediately appears as booked to all other users on the next availability read (no stale cache). |
| **AC-12** | All three workflows are reachable end-to-end with the exact wording in Section 3. |

---

## 6. Assumptions (explicit, pending user answers)

Made so the developer is not blocked. Each maps to a chat question above; all are cheap to change if the user replies.

| # | Question | Assumed default |
|---|---|---|
| A1 | Rooms & capacities | 3 seed rooms: `Small (4)`, `Medium (8)`, `Large (12)`; same hours. Data-driven, so easily replaced. |
| A2 | Granularity | Fixed **30-minute slots**; bookings are start/end on slot boundaries. |
| A3 | Working hours / timezone | Bookable **09:00–18:00, Mon–Fri**, in **Asia/Hong_Kong (UTC+8)**; all times stored in **UTC**. |
| A4 | Max duration | **4 hours** per booking. |
| A5 | Cancellation authority | **Organiser or admin only**; `cancel_reason` **optional**. |
| A6 | Recurring bookings | **Not supported in v1** (single bookings only). |
| A7 | Overlap/back-to-back | **Back-to-back allowed**; only true overlaps forbidden (R1). |
| A8 | Team model | **Multi-team, single shared dataset**, no per-team isolation or approval. |

> ⚠️ If any answer contradicts a default, the affected section (2, 3, 4, or 5) is updated and this table is marked resolved. Assumptions A1–A8 are **configuration-level**, so no code rewrite is required to change them.

---

## 7. Downstream hand-off

- **Developer:** implement entities per Section 2, the atomic overlap guard per R1, and the synchronous cancellation per R2; expose WF-1/WF-2/WF-3 exactly as worded.
- **Tester:** treat Section 5 as the test plan; AC-4 requires a **concurrency** test, AC-6 a **partial-overlap matrix**, AC-7/AC-8 the **no-stale-record** checks.

---

**Deliverable status:** Complete as an inline markdown document. Open questions posted to the team (top of message); all defaults documented (Section 6) so development and testing can start immediately. Once the user answers, I will reconcile Sections 2–6 against their replies and hand a frozen v1.0 to the developer.

# Meeting Room Booking — How to Use It (and What Was Built)

## What it is / what it replaces
A small program that replaces our shared spreadsheet. It removes the two problems we had:
- **Double bookings** — a room+time slot can hold only ONE confirmed booking; any overlap is rejected.
- **Stale records** — cancelling a booking instantly frees its slot, so availability is always current.
No installation needed (Python 3 only). Data survives restarts.

## Start it (exact command)
    cd sandboxes/258c8916685642f3a261281a8ffde149
    python3 main.py
Menu: 1) Check availability  2) Book a room  3) Cancel a booking  4) List bookings  5) Quit
**Data is stored in `bookings.db`** (SQLite) next to `main.py`. Seeded rooms: Boardroom (12), Meeting Room A (8), Huddle Room B (4).

## Rules in effect
- Rooms: Boardroom, Meeting Room A, Huddle Room B.
- Working hours 09:00–18:00, Monday–Friday (Hong Kong time). No past dates; up to 365 days ahead.
- 30-minute slots; times must be on a :00 or :30 boundary. Max booking length 4 hours.
- No-overlap: rejected if it overlaps a *confirmed* booking in the same room. Back-to-back is allowed.
- Who can cancel: anyone can cancel any booking by its id (no login/owner check — see Assumptions).

## Step-by-step walkthrough
1) **Check availability**
       python3 main.py show --date 2026-10-05
       python3 main.py show --date 2026-10-05 --room "Boardroom"
   Each 30-min slot prints `free` or `[X] ... TAKEN - booking #N: <purpose> (<name>)`.
2) **Book a room**
       python3 main.py book --date 2026-10-05 --room "Boardroom" --start 10:00 --end 11:00 --title "Sprint review" --organiser "Alice"
   → `SUCCESS: booking #1 confirmed - Boardroom (Sprint review) on 2026-10-05, 10:00-11:00 for Alice`
   Re-running with an overlapping time, e.g. `--start 10:30 --end 11:30`, is REJECTED:
   → `ERROR: Overlap: Boardroom is already booked 10:00-11:00 on 2026-10-05 by Alice (booking #1). Choose another slot or cancel that booking first.`
3) **Cancel a booking**
       python3 main.py cancel --id 1
       python3 main.py cancel --room "Boardroom" --date 2026-10-05
   → `SUCCESS: booking #1 cancelled - Boardroom on 2026-10-05, 10:00-11:00. The slot is now free.`
   A follow-up `show` prints `10:00-10:30  free` and `10:30-11:00  free`.

Errors print `ERROR: <text>` (exit code 1); `SUCCESS` means it worked.

- `Overlap: <room> is already booked ... (booking #N)` — slot taken; pick another time or cancel #N first.
- `Bookings must be within working hours 09:00-18:00.` — time outside the day.
- `... must be on a 30-minute boundary` — use :00 or :30.
- `Booking too long ... maximum is 240 minutes (4 hours).` — shorten it.
- `End time ... must be after start time.` — swap start/end.
- `Date ... is in the past.` / `more than 365 days in the future.` — pick a valid date.
- `Date ... is a Saturday - rooms may only be booked Monday to Friday.` — pick a weekday.

# Meeting Room Booking System — Requirements Specification (v0.1)

**Status:** Draft · **Owner:** Technical Lead · **Date:** 2026-11 · **Applies to:** v1 (single shared dataset)

> **How to read this document.** This is the single source of truth for the build. Sections 1–2 define data; Section 3 gives the exact, verbatim workflow wording the UI and the tests must use; Section 4 states the two hard, non-negotiable rules; Section 5 gives acceptance criteria the tester will verify; Section 6 records assumptions made pending user answers. Nothing here blocks development — every open question has a stated default.

---

## 1. Scope

Replace the team's shared spreadsheet with a booking system that (a) always shows accurate availability, (b) prevents double bookings, and (c) removes a slot the moment a booking is cancelled. The spreadsheet's two failure modes — double bookings and stale records after cancellation — are the primary defects this system must eliminate.

**In scope (v1):** check availability, make a booking, cancel a booking, single shared dataset across teams.
**Out of scope (v1):** recurring bookings, per-team isolation/authentication tiers, room equipment inventory management, calendar invites/notifications, approvals workflow.

---

## 2. Core entities

### 2.1 Room

| Field | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string (slug/uuid) | yes | Stable, unique, immutable. |
| `name` | string | yes | Human-readable, unique. |
| `capacity` | integer > 0 | yes | Max attendees. |
| `location` | string | no | e.g. floor/building. |
| `amenities` | list of string | no | e.g. `["projector","whiteboard"]`; defaults to `[]`. |
| `active` | boolean | yes | Default `true`. Inactive rooms are hidden from booking but existing bookings remain valid. |

### 2.2 Booking

| Field | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string (uuid) | yes | Assigned by system. |
| `room_id` | reference → Room.id | yes | Must reference an active room at creation time. |
| `title` | string | yes | Purpose of the meeting. |
| `organiser` | string (email/ID) | yes | The person who booked. |
| `attendees` | integer ≥ 1 | no | Default `1`; must be ≤ room capacity (warning, see AC-8). |
| `start` | datetime (ISO-8601, UTC, slot-aligned) | yes | Inclusive start of the half-open interval. |
| `end` | datetime (ISO-8601, UTC, slot-aligned) | yes | Exclusive end; must be `> start`. |
| `status` | enum: `confirmed` \| `cancelled` | yes | Default `confirmed`. |
| `created_at` | datetime (UTC) | yes | Set by system. |
| `cancelled_at` | datetime (UTC) \| null | no | Set when status becomes `cancelled`. |
| `cancel_reason` | string \| null | no | Optional (pending Q5). |
| `cancelled_by` | string \| null | no | Who performed the cancellation. |

**Interval convention (fixed, do not change):** a booking occupies the **half-open interval `[start, end)`**. Two intervals overlap **iff** `a.start < b.end AND b.start < a.end`. This convention is what makes back-to-back bookings legal (see Rule R1).

---

## 3. User workflows (exact wording)

These three strings are the canonical descriptions. UI copy and test names must match the intent exactly.

### WF-1 — Check availability
> **"Check availability":** the user selects a room and a date (or a time range) and sees every bookable slot for that room on that day, each slot marked as **available** or **booked**. A slot is shown as available if and only if no booking with status `confirmed` covers it. Cancelled bookings must never appear as blocking.

### WF-2 — Book a room
> **"Book a room":** the user picks an available slot for a room, enters a title and organiser (and optionally attendees), and confirms. If the slot is still free at confirmation time, the system creates a `confirmed` booking and the slot immediately shows as booked for everyone else. If the slot is no longer free, the system refuses the booking with a clear conflict message and creates nothing.

### WF-3 — Cancel a booking
> **"Cancel a booking":** the user opens an existing booking and cancels it (optionally giving a reason, if permitted). After cancellation the booking's status becomes `cancelled` and its slot is **immediately** shown as available again in WF-1 for every user.

---

## 4. Hard rules (non-negotiable)

- **R1 — No overlapping confirmed bookings.** For the same room, two bookings with status `confirmed` may **never** overlap in time: for any two such bookings `a`, `b` where `a.room_id == b.room_id`, it must hold that `NOT (a.start < b.end AND b.start < a.end)`. Back-to-back bookings (`a.end == b.start`) are **allowed**. The check must be enforced **atomically at write time** so two simultaneous requests cannot both succeed (no check-then-write race). On failure the system returns a conflict error and persists nothing.
- **R2 — Cancellation frees the slot immediately; no stale records.** A cancelled booking must free its slot synchronously: any availability query (WF-1) issued *after* a cancellation returns must show that slot as available, with no delay, cache, or background reconciliation. Cancelled bookings are retained only as history and must be excluded from every availability/blocking view. There must be no state in which a cancelled booking blocks a slot.

---

## 5. Acceptance criteria

Testable criteria; the tester verifies each against WF-1/WF-2/WF-3 and R1/R2.

| ID | Criterion |
|---|---|
| **AC-1** | Availability (WF-1) lists exactly the slots in the room's working hours, each marked available/booked correctly. |
| **AC-2** | A booking whose `[start,end)` does not overlap any confirmed booking for that room is created with status `confirmed`. |
| **AC-3 (R1)** | A booking attempt that would overlap an existing confirmed booking for the same room is rejected with a conflict error and persists **zero** records. |
| **AC-4 (R1)** | Two confirmed bookings for the same room can never be in an overlapping state — verified by concurrent booking attempts, where at most one succeeds. |
| **AC-5 (R1)** | Back-to-back bookings (`a.end == b.start`) are **accepted**. |
| **AC-6 (R1)** | Partial overlaps (start inside another, end inside another, one fully contained) are all **rejected**. |
| **AC-7 (R2)** | After a cancellation, a subsequent WF-1 call shows the freed slot as available immediately (same request cycle; no wait). |
| **AC-8** | A cancelled booking never blocks any future booking of the same room and never appears as "booked" in availability. |
| **AC-9 (WF-3)** | Cancelling sets `status=cancelled` and records `cancelled_at`; the record is retained for history but excluded from blocking views. |
| **AC-10** | `end > start` is enforced; `start`/`end` are slot-aligned and stored in UTC; `attendees ≤ capacity` produces a warning (not a hard block) when configured as such. |
| **AC-11 (WF-2)** | A successful booking immediately appears as booked to all other users on the next availability read (no stale cache). |
| **AC-12** | All three workflows are reachable end-to-end with the exact wording in Section 3. |

---

## 6. Assumptions (explicit, pending user answers)

Made so the developer is not blocked. Each maps to a chat question above; all are cheap to change if the user replies.

| # | Question | Assumed default |
|---|---|---|
| A1 | Rooms & capacities | 3 seed rooms: `Small (4)`, `Medium (8)`, `Large (12)`; same hours. Data-driven, so easily replaced. |
| A2 | Granularity | Fixed **30-minute slots**; bookings are start/end on slot boundaries. |
| A3 | Working hours / timezone | Bookable **09:00–18:00, Mon–Fri**, in **Asia/Hong_Kong (UTC+8)**; all times stored in **UTC**. |
| A4 | Max duration | **4 hours** per booking. |
| A5 | Cancellation authority | **Organiser or admin only**; `cancel_reason` **optional**. |
| A6 | Recurring bookings | **Not supported in v1** (single bookings only). |
| A7 | Overlap/back-to-back | **Back-to-back allowed**; only true overlaps forbidden (R1). |
| A8 | Team model | **Multi-team, single shared dataset**, no per-team isolation or approval. |

> ⚠️ If any answer contradicts a default, the affected section (2, 3, 4, or 5) is updated and this table is marked resolved. Assumptions A1–A8 are **configuration-level**, so no code rewrite is required to change them.

---

## 7. Downstream hand-off

- **Developer:** implement entities per Section 2, the atomic overlap guard per R1, and the synchronous cancellation per R2; expose WF-1/WF-2/WF-3 exactly as worded.
- **Tester:** treat Section 5 as the test plan; AC-4 requires a **concurrency** test, AC-6 a **partial-overlap matrix**, AC-7/AC-8 the **no-stale-record** checks.

## Defects found (from source inspection; **not** runtime-confirmed)

> All reproduction steps below are **static** — the step "run and observe the message" was not executed. Error strings are quoted verbatim *from the source*, not from an observed run.

**D1 — MEDIUM — Overlap check is not atomic; parallel requests can double-book.**
`book_room` selects confirmed bookings, then inserts, with no unique constraint and no `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`/transaction guard (`confirmed_bookings` + `INSERT` are separate statements; only `conn.commit()` after). Two concurrent `book` invocations for the same room/slot can both pass the check and both insert, reproducing exactly the double-booking the team complained about.
*Repro (planned):* fire two `python3 main.py book … --start 10:00 --end 11:00` for the same room/date in parallel; inspect `list`. *Observed:* not executed.

**D2 — LOW — Availability and booking silently require a future weekday, so "today" can be uncheckable.**
`parse_date` (used by both `check_availability` and `book_room`) rejects past dates and any non-Mon–Fri date. A user cannot view availability for today if today falls on a weekend, nor for a past date — a mild usability gap vs. a plain "check availability" expectation. *Observed:* not executed.

**D3 — LOW — Argument parser can mis-handle empty/edge values.**
`parse_args` treats a following token starting with `--` (or a missing token) as an empty value (`val = ""`) and then advances only one position. An intentionally empty value, or any value that itself starts with `--`, is silently swallowed. *Observed:* not executed.

**D4 — INFO — Cancelled bookings still appear in `list` by default.**
`list_bookings(include_cancelled=True)` is the default and the menu never passes `False`, so cancelled records are shown alongside confirmed ones. This is a deliberate "keep for the record" choice (documented in README) but can confuse users who expect cancelled entries to disappear — the original pain point was "records not updated after cancellations." *Observed:* not executed.

# Meeting Room Booking — How to Use It (and What Was Built)

## What it is / what it replaces
A small program that replaces our shared spreadsheet. It removes the two problems we had:
- **Double bookings** — a room+time slot can hold only ONE confirmed booking; any overlap is rejected.
- **Stale records** — cancelling a booking instantly frees its slot, so availability is always current.
No installation needed (Python 3 only). Data survives restarts.

## Start it (exact command)
    cd sandboxes/258c8916685642f3a261281a8ffde149
    python3 main.py
Menu: 1) Check availability  2) Book a room  3) Cancel a booking  4) List bookings  5) Quit
**Data is stored in `bookings.db`** (SQLite) next to `main.py`. Seeded rooms: Boardroom (12), Meeting Room A (8), Huddle Room B (4).

## Rules in effect
- Rooms: Boardroom, Meeting Room A, Huddle Room B.
- Working hours 09:00–18:00, Monday–Friday (Hong Kong time). No past dates; up to 365 days ahead.
- 30-minute slots; times must be on a :00 or :30 boundary. Max booking length 4 hours.
- No-overlap: rejected if it overlaps a *confirmed* booking in the same room. Back-to-back is allowed.
- Who can cancel: anyone can cancel any booking by its id (no login/owner check — see Assumptions).

## Step-by-step walkthrough
1) **Check availability**
       python3 main.py show --date 2026-10-05
       python3 main.py show --date 2026-10-05 --room "Boardroom"
   Each 30-min slot prints `free` or `[X] ... TAKEN - booking #N: <purpose> (<name>)`.
2) **Book a room**
       python3 main.py book --date 2026-10-05 --room "Boardroom" --start 10:00 --end 11:00 --title "Sprint review" --organiser "Alice"
   → `SUCCESS: booking #1 confirmed - Boardroom (Sprint review) on 2026-10-05, 10:00-11:00 for Alice`
   Re-running with an overlapping time, e.g. `--start 10:30 --end 11:30`, is REJECTED:
   → `ERROR: Overlap: Boardroom is already booked 10:00-11:00 on 2026-10-05 by Alice (booking #1). Choose another slot or cancel that booking first.`
3) **Cancel a booking**
       python3 main.py cancel --id 1
       python3 main.py cancel --room "Boardroom" --date 2026-10-05
   → `SUCCESS: booking #1 cancelled - Boardroom on 2026-10-05, 10:00-11:00. The slot is now free.`
   A follow-up `show` prints `10:00-10:30  free` and `10:30-11:00  free`.
Extras: `python3 main.py list` (all), `list --date 2026-10-05`.

## Error messages — what they mean and what to do
Errors print `ERROR: <text>` (exit code 1); `SUCCESS` means it worked.
- `Unknown room ... Available rooms: ...` — misspelt name; use one of the three.
- `Overlap: <room> is already booked ... (booking #N)` — slot taken; pick another time or cancel #N first.
- `Bookings must be within working hours 09:00-18:00.` — time outside the day.
- `... must be on a 30-minute boundary` — use :00 or :30.
- `Booking too long ... maximum is 240 minutes (4 hours).` — shorten it.
- `End time ... must be after start time.` — swap start/end.
- `Date ... is in the past.` / `more than 365 days in the future.` — pick a valid date.
- `Date ... is a Saturday - rooms may only be booked Monday to Friday.` — pick a weekday.
- `No booking with id X.` / `Booking #X is already cancelled.` / `Multiple confirmed bookings ... use cancel --id <id>.` — fix the cancel input.

## Out of scope / assumptions (from unanswered clarification questions)
- Anyone can cancel any booking (no per-user login, permissions, or owner check) — assumed OK.
- Not built: recurring bookings, attendee/invite lists, email/Slack reminders, approval workflow, admin UI to add rooms.
- Rooms fixed to the 3 seeded ones (change `SEED_ROOMS`, delete `bookings.db` to reset).
- One shared database file: fine for a small team, not a hardened multi-user server.
- Fixed defaults: 365-day horizon, 4-hour max, timezone Asia/Hong_Kong (UTC+8).
